subject: Reservation MAP & evaluation checkpoints — proposed timeline for Veridian Health
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Chen <sally.chen@veridianhealth.com>, ops@veridianhealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reservation MAP & evaluation checkpoints — proposed timeline for Veridian Health

Sally / Veridian team —

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. Attached is a first-draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and the sizing model we used to produce the GPU pool recommendations. High-level ask: can you review the timeline and acceptance criteria, and confirm the procurement windows for your procurement and infra teams so we can lock in Dedicated vs Private options?

Summary (short):
- Target close window: 10/25–11/05 (customer-side approvals + PO)
- Goal: Reserve a Dedicated GPU pool (H100 equivalent) with Private deployment option as fallback
- Suggested initial pool: 8 reserved accelerators, burst to 16 for peak evals (see sizing spreadsheet)
- Key checkpoints: evaluation pass (latency & perf) by 10/20, SOC2 evidence for Private by 10/22, PO signed by 11/02

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Veridian confirms procurement lead and earliest PO date (procurement@veridianhealth.com)
2) We run an acceptance-run test on 10/18–10/19 (our env) using the attached acceptance-test-checklist.pdf
3) If acceptance passes, Redwood will mark capacity for Veridian and begin procurement placement (lead times noted in MAP)

Open questions we flagged internally:
- Do you require quantized model variants (4-bit/8-bit) for cost planning? That changes expected throughput and slot sizing.
- For Private (on-prem), what is your timeline for network/firewall approval?

I've attached: Veridian_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestones), gpu_pool_sizing_model.csv (assumptions), acceptance-test-checklist.pdf.

Can we lock a 30-minute alignment call for Wednesday 10/13? I dropped a tentative at the link below.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: Veridian_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx), gpu_pool_sizing_model.csv (csv), acceptance-test-checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Sally Chen <sally.chen@veridianhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@veridianhealth.com, procurement@veridianhealth.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reservation MAP & evaluation checkpoints — proposed timeline for Veridian Health

Neha —

Thanks for the clear doc and sizing model. A few quick notes from our side after reviewing with infra and procurement:

- Procurement can target a PO on or before 11/01, but we need final pricing and confirmation of reserved capacity before 10/22 to include in our internal approval packet.
- Infra wants clarity on whether the acceptance test will be run against a Dedicated reserved pool or a short-term burst allocation. Latency targets are strict: p95 < 120ms for 2k token sequences.
- We will need SOC2 artifacts (scope and date) by 10/22 to proceed with Private onboarding. Can Redwood provide the audit summary and the attestating contact?

On quantization: we plan to test both float and 8-bit variants during evaluation. If Redwood can provide per-token cost estimates for each quantization profile (in the MAP spreadsheet), that would help our TCO assessment.

I think the 8-reserve, burst-to-16 plan makes sense as long as the acceptance tests are run wholly on the reserved pool for determinism.

We can take the 10/13 call; I will include our procurement lead (procurement@veridianhealth.com) on the calendar.

Sally Chen
Head of Infrastructure, Veridian Health
sally.chen@veridianhealth.com

Subject: Re: Reservation MAP & evaluation checkpoints — proposed timeline for Veridian Health

Neha / team —

Quick internal note and suggested tactical updates before the 10/13 alignment call:

- GPU sizing: the attached model presumes ~65% average utilization during eval windows. For Veridian's latency target (p95 < 120ms at 2k tokens) I recommend we size conservatively: 10 reserved units for the initial lane, with explicit burst policy to 18 for the two-week evaluation (this gives headroom for batch-peaks and avoids noisy-neighbor queuing).
- Procurement lead time: Dedicated (hosted) placement lead time is currently 18–22 business days from placement; Private (VPC/on-prem) requires firewall cert + SOC2 gate which can add 3–4 weeks. We should include both timelines in the MAP and tie rollback windows to them.
- Acceptance tests: propose we run deterministic perf tests on a dedicated reservation (not burst) for the official acceptance step; run parallel quantized cost runs on burst to produce TCO estimates. Add fields in the MAP for test IDs and dataset references.

Action items for this thread (my proposals):
A) Update MAP: reserve_count -> 10, burst_cap -> 18, add procurement lead-time rows (Dedicated 18bd / Private 28bd)
B) Neha: circulate updated MAP + per-quantization cost rows by EOD 10/13
C) Ben: confirm commercial flex for a short-term burst credit if Private onboarding slips beyond 11/15

Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Sally / procurement / ops —

Thanks for the quick replies and alignment. Per Karthik's suggestion I updated the MAP and sizing model (attached) with conservative reserve_count and explicit lead times. Key updates/confirmations below:

- Reserve: 10 units; burst cap -> 18 for evaluation window
- Lead times: Dedicated 18 business days, Private (on-prem) 28 business days once SOC2 & firewall rules are approved
- Acceptance: perf verification on reserved Dedicated pool (p95 < 120ms at 2k tokens) + functional checks in acceptance-test-checklist.pdf
- Documentation: SOC2 audit summary and auditor contact: redwood-audit@redwood.ai (summary attached as part of SOC2 bundle)

Next steps:
1) Procurement to confirm earliest PO date (procurement@veridianhealth.com) — requested by 2026-10-22 so we can place reservations by 10/25.
2) I scheduled a 30-minute alignment call: https://calendar.redwood.com/meet/30m/align-20261013 (please accept/modify)
3) Karthik and Ben will stand by for commercial flex requests for burst credits if Private onboarding slips.

If that all looks good, I'll mark this MAP as v1.1 and prepare contract paperwork for the Dedicated reservation option and a Private fallback addendum.

Thanks —
